content.title: About
content.content: Empanada, beef, with vegetables is a traditional Spanish‑Latin American pastry made from thin dough filled with seasoned ground beef, carrots, sweet pepper and onion. The dough is usually fried until golden, giving a crisp exterior and a juicy interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word empanada comes from “empanar,” meaning “to wrap in dough.”
In different countries the filling may include cheese, chicken, seafood or even sweet fruit.
Empanadas are traditionally served at holidays and family celebrations, especially in Argentina and Chile.
The dough often contains wheat flour, butter and a small amount of yeast, which makes it light and airy.
One theory says empanadas were first made in Spain during colonization and later adapted in South America.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Ground beef provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and vegetables supply B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Carrots and sweet pepper add dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Vegetables contain beta‑carotene and vitamin C, helping combat free radicals.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Using fatty ground beef or deep‑frying the pastry can make the dish calorie‑dense.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The wheat‑based dough contains gluten, which may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Added salt in the filling can increase sodium intake, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Potential pathogens
items.content: Beef must be cooked thoroughly to avoid risks of salmonella or other food‑borne infections.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Empanadas are served hot as a snack or main dish, accompanied by salsa, sour cream or guacamole. They are easy to eat with hands, breaking them into bite‑size pieces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked empanadas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a bag for up to 2 months and reheat in the oven until crisp.
